description: Start the FastAPI/uvicorn HTTPS callback server that handles the Google OAuth redirect. Must be running before the operator completes the browser flow. A local solet defaults to explicit IPv4 loopback (127.0.0.1); an ALB-fronted cloud deployment must configure 0.0.0.0 explicitly and routes /oauth/google/* by path rule to this task's port. Returns the bound host, port, and callback URL.
embedding_description: Launch the Google Workspace OAuth redirect listener before connect_account. Serves GET /oauth/google/callback, validates state and PKCE, exchanges the authorization code, and vaults tokens. Local default: 127.0.0.1. For ALB-fronted cloud, explicitly bind 0.0.0.0 and route /oauth/google/* to this port. Returns host, port, callback_url.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dict with the bound host, allocated port, and callback URL.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Confirm the callback server is listening and state the callback_url. Note that connect_account can now be run.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Start the Google OAuth callback uvicorn server.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: service_not_available: the vault or address-book service the callback needs was not injected at readiness. callback_server_start_failed: the uvicorn server could not bind its socket within the five-second startup window — almost always another process already listening on that port, occasionally a host the process may not bind. The message carries the host, the port, and the underlying bind error.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: service_not_available: confirm the plugin reached readiness (vault + address_book bound). Check plugin load logs; retry after the platform is fully started. callback_server_start_failed: find what already holds the port (lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN), then either stop that process or call start_interface again with an explicit free port. Never treat this error as cosmetic — the callback server is NOT listening, so the Google redirect would land on whatever else owns the port and the browser flow cannot complete.
